questions.question_text: Isaac is solving a problem about rolling a die. What does $P(3)$ mean?

options.why: $P$ stands for probability, not for the number of rolls of the die.

options.text: The number of $3$s that were rolled
options.why: $P(3)$ is a probability between $0$ and $1$, not a count of results.
$P(3)$ describes one roll of one die; the $3$ names the event, not the number of dice.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{event})$ means 'the probability of the event happening'.
$P(3)$ is the probability of rolling a $3$.

questions.question_text: A standard six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number less than $3$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Counts $1$, $2$ and $3$ as favourable, but 'less than $3$' does not include $3$.
Counts only one favourable outcome, but both $1$ and $2$ are less than $3$.
Counts the outcomes that are $3$ or more instead of those less than $3$.

questions.solution_text:
There are $6$ equally likely outcomes.
The favourable outcomes are $\{1, 2\}$.
$P(\text{less than } 3) = \frac{2}{6}$
$= \frac{1}{3}$

options.why: Counts the $3$ green sectors instead of the $2$ red sectors.
Counts only $1$ red sector, but red covers $2$ of the $6$ sectors.
Counts the $4$ sectors that are not red instead of the red sectors.

questions.solution_text:
The $6$ sectors are equal, so there are $6$ equally likely outcomes.
Red covers $2$ sectors.
$P(R) = \frac{2}{6}$
$= \frac{1}{3}$

questions.question_text: A jar contains $8$ blue, $4$ orange and $6$ red marbles. One marble is picked at random. What is $P(\text{orange})$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Uses the $8$ blue marbles as the favourable count instead of the $4$ orange marbles.
Divides by the $14$ marbles that are not orange instead of by all $18$ marbles.
Uses the $6$ red marbles as the favourable count instead of the $4$ orange marbles.

questions.solution_text:
There are $8 + 4 + 6 = 18$ marbles, so there are $18$ equally likely outcomes.
$P(\text{orange}) = \frac{4}{18}$
$= \frac{2}{9}$

questions.question_text: A bag contains $3$ red, $2$ green and $5$ blue marbles. One marble is chosen at random. What is $P(\text{green})$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Treats the three colours as equally likely, but the equally likely outcomes are the $10$ marbles.
Divides by the $8$ marbles that are not green instead of by all $10$ marbles.
Divides the $2$ green marbles by the $5$ blue marbles instead of by all $10$ marbles.

questions.solution_text:
There are $3 + 2 + 5 = 10$ marbles, so there are $10$ equally likely outcomes.
$P(\text{green}) = \frac{2}{10}$
$= \frac{1}{5}$

questions.question_text: Box A contains $3$ red marbles and $6$ green marbles. Box B contains $2$ red marbles and $4$ green marbles. One marble is drawn at random from each box. From which box are you more likely to draw a red marble?

options.text: Both boxes give the same chance
Box A, because it has more red marbles
options.why: Box A also has more marbles in total; both probabilities simplify to the same fraction.

options.text: Box B, because it has fewer marbles in total
options.why: Box B also has fewer red marbles; both probabilities simplify to the same fraction.

options.text: It cannot be decided without running an experiment
options.why: Theoretical probability is calculated from the counts, so no experiment is needed.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{red from A}) = \frac{3}{9}$
$= \frac{1}{3}$
$P(\text{red from B}) = \frac{2}{6}$
$= \frac{1}{3}$
The probabilities are equal, so both boxes give the same chance of red.

questions.question_text: The letters of the word SUCCESS are written on $7$ cards and placed in a hat. One card is drawn at random. What is $P(\text{S})$?

options.why: Treats the four different letters in the sample space as equally likely, but the outcomes are the $7$ cards.
Divides the $3$ S cards by the $4$ letters in the sample space instead of by the $7$ cards.
Counts the $4$ cards that are not S instead of the $3$ cards that are.

questions.solution_text:
There are $7$ cards, so there are $7$ equally likely outcomes.
The letter S appears on $3$ cards.
$P(\text{S}) = \frac{3}{7}$

questions.question_text: A fair twelve-sided die has its faces numbered from $1$ to $12$. It is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than $9$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Counts $9$, $10$, $11$ and $12$ as favourable, but 'greater than $9$' does not include $9$.
Counts only $11$ and $12$, leaving out $10$, which is also greater than $9$.
Counts the outcomes that are $9$ or less instead of those greater than $9$.

questions.solution_text:
There are $12$ equally likely outcomes.
The favourable outcomes are $\{10, 11, 12\}$.
$P(\text{greater than } 9) = \frac{3}{12}$
$= \frac{1}{4}$

questions.question_text: A jar contains $6$ red, $4$ green, $7$ yellow and $3$ blue marbles. One marble is selected at random. What is $P(\text{red})$, as a percentage?

options.why: Uses the $7$ yellow marbles as the favourable count instead of the $6$ red marbles.
Writes the favourable count itself as a percentage instead of dividing by the $20$ marbles first.
Uses the $4$ green marbles as the favourable count instead of the $6$ red marbles.

questions.solution_text:
There are $6 + 4 + 7 + 3 = 20$ marbles, so there are $20$ equally likely outcomes.
$P(\text{red}) = \frac{6}{20}$
$= \frac{30}{100}$
$= 30\%$
